findings.title: Vital reschedule does not wait for calendar or video deletion
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) does not await its callbacks, and the try/catch around it cannot see rejections from them. getCalendar is now async, so calendar.deleteEvent is not even started until that import resolves, and neither deleteEvent nor deleteMeeting is awaited. Reschedule then sends the reschedule email and returns true while the external calendar event and video meeting may still exist. On serverless, the handler can be frozen after the response, so the cleanup often never runs and the old slot stays busy. Failures become unhandled promise rejections. Replace this with await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) and await both deleteEvent and deleteMeeting inside the mapper.

findings.title: WipeMyCal reschedule does not wait for calendar or video deletion
findings.body: The same forEach(async) pattern was introduced here when getCalendar became async. Array.forEach ignores the promises returned by async callbacks, so the try/catch never observes getCalendar, deleteEvent, or deleteMeeting failures, and the function sends the reschedule email and returns true without waiting for those calls. Because the first await is now the dynamic app import, deletion is no longer even initiated before the handler continues. Serverless runtimes can freeze after the response and drop that work, leaving the cancelled event on the user's calendar and the slot blocked. Await Promise.all over a map, and await deleteEvent and deleteMeeting inside it.

findings.title: requestReschedule returns before calendar and video cleanup
findings.body: requestReschedule now uses bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) so it can await getCalendar, but forEach does not wait for those promises. The mutation marks the booking CANCELLED, sends the reschedule email, fires BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks, and resolves while calendar.deleteEvent and deleteMeeting may not have started. Previously getCalendar was synchronous, so deleteEvent was at least invoked before the handler continued. Now the first await yields before any provider call, and a serverless isolate can exit before the dynamic import finishes. Rejected imports or delete failures are unhandled rejections with no surrounding try/catch. Collect the work with await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) and await both deleteEvent and deleteMeeting before sending email or returning.

findings.title: Recurring cancel races calendar deletion against Promise.all
findings.body: When cancelling all remaining instances of a recurring event, credentials are still walked with forEach(async), and this change added await getCalendar inside that callback before deleteEvent. forEach does not wait, and apiDeletes.push only happens after both awaits, so the later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) (around line 652) usually runs while apiDeletes still lacks these deletions — often before deleteEvent has been called at all. The non-recurring else branch just below was correctly rewritten to a for-loop that awaits getCalendar and pushes the delete promise before continuing; the recurring branch was not. The handler can therefore return success while series events remain on the external calendar and those times stay busy. Errors in the callback are unhandled rejections. Await Promise.all on the credential list (and on each deleteEvent) instead of forEach, and push the promises before awaiting them if they must be included in apiDeletes.
